hero.title: Specialists and emergency care,
hero.description: A specialty hospital in northern Aguascalientes: 24-hour emergency room, inpatient care, intensive care, surgery and over 50 medical specialists, without traveling to the state capital.

servicesSection.title: Services and
servicesSection.description: Emergency care, inpatient care, surgery and diagnostics under one roof, in the north of the state.

urgencias.name: 24-Hour Emergency Room
urgencias.desc: Medical and surgical emergency care 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
urgencias.full: Our emergency room is open day and night for medical, surgical, obstetric and pediatric emergencies. We have observation beds and the support of the laboratory, imaging, blood bank, surgical area and intensive care within the same hospital.

process.title: Arrival and assessment
process.desc: When you arrive, our staff assesses your condition so the most serious cases are seen first.

process.title: Care and tests
process.desc: The emergency physician treats you and, if needed, orders lab work or imaging in the same hospital.

process.title: Discharge or admission
process.desc: Depending on how you respond, you go home with instructions or are admitted to continue treatment.

faq.q: Do I need an appointment for the emergency room?
faq.a: No. The emergency room sees patients without an appointment, 24 hours a day, every day of the year.

faq.q: Do you treat emergencies for children and pregnant women?
faq.a: Yes. We have pediatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, and neonatal intensive care in the hospital.

faq.q: What should I do in a serious emergency?
faq.a: If the person can't be moved, call 911. If they can be moved safely, come directly to our emergency room.

hospitalizacion.name: Inpatient Care
hospitalizacion.desc: Private rooms with round-the-clock medical and nursing care.
hospitalizacion.full: When you need to stay in the hospital, you're admitted to a private room with 24-hour nursing care and follow-up from your attending physician. Your stay is supported by the pharmacy, laboratory and imaging within the hospital.

process.title: Admission
process.desc: The admissions team registers your information and assigns your room.

process.title: Care during your stay
process.desc: Nursing staff monitors you around the clock and your attending physician follows your progress.

process.title: Discharge
process.desc: Your doctor authorizes discharge and gives you instructions to continue recovering at home.

faq.q: Are the rooms private?
faq.a: Yes. Every inpatient has their own room.

faq.q: Can my own doctor admit me?
faq.a: Medipab works with independent medical specialists. If your doctor practices at the hospital, they can admit you and follow up here — just ask us.

faq.q: What should I bring for my hospital stay?
faq.a: Official ID, your previous test results and prescriptions, a list of the medications you take, and personal hygiene items.

terapia-intensiva.name: Adult Intensive Care (ICU)
terapia-intensiva.desc: Intensive care unit for critically ill adult patients.
terapia-intensiva.full: The Intensive Care Unit treats adult patients who need continuous monitoring and support of their vital functions, whether due to a serious illness, a complication or major surgery. Our medical and nursing team monitors every patient at all times.

process.title: Admission to the unit
process.desc: Patients arrive from the emergency room, operating room or inpatient floor when their condition requires it.

process.title: Continuous monitoring
process.desc: Constant monitoring of vital signs and treatment adjustments by the intensive care team.

process.title: Transfer to a room
process.desc: Once the patient is stable, recovery continues in an inpatient room.

faq.q: How do I get updates on my family member?
faq.a: The medical team updates family members on the patient's progress. Ask at the unit about update and visiting hours.

faq.q: Who decides admission to intensive care?
faq.a: A physician orders the admission, usually from the emergency room, operating room or inpatient floor, depending on the patient's condition.

neonatologia-ucin.name: Neonatology and NICU
neonatologia-ucin.desc: Neonatal intensive care for premature or at-risk newborns.
neonatologia-ucin.full: The Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) cares for newborns who need special monitoring: premature babies, low-birth-weight babies or those with a complication at birth. Because the unit is in the same hospital where they're born, they receive specialized care from the very first moment.
conditions: Monitoring of babies from high-risk pregnancies

process.title: Care at birth
process.desc: The team assesses the baby from birth and decides whether special monitoring is needed.

process.title: NICU care
process.desc: Continuous monitoring, feeding and treatment tailored to each baby's needs.

process.title: Discharge and follow-up
process.desc: Once the baby is stable, we teach you how to care for them and schedule pediatric follow-up.

faq.q: Will my baby need the NICU?
faq.a: Most newborns don't. The physician decides at birth based on the baby's health.

faq.q: Can I visit my baby?
faq.a: Yes. The unit staff will tell you how and when you can be with your baby, following the unit's hygiene measures.

ginecologia-obstetricia.name: Obstetrics and Gynecology
ginecologia-obstetricia.desc: Prenatal care, labor and C-section delivery, and women's health.
ginecologia-obstetricia.full: We care for women at every stage: gynecological consultations, prenatal care, and labor or C-section delivery at the hospital, with pediatrics and neonatal intensive care available for the newborn.

process.title: First visit
process.desc: Medical history, physical exam and initial tests if needed.

process.title: Pregnancy follow-up
process.desc: Regular visits with lab work and imaging depending on the stage of your pregnancy.

process.title: Birth
process.desc: Vaginal delivery or C-section at the hospital, with pediatrics ready to receive your baby.

faq.q: Do you handle obstetric emergencies?
faq.a: Yes. Our emergency room is open 24 hours a day, every day.

faq.q: What if my baby is born with a complication?
faq.a: We have a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit in the same hospital, so your baby receives specialized care from the very first moment.

pediatria.name: Pediatrics
pediatria.desc: Medical care for babies, children and teenagers.
pediatria.full: We care for your children from birth through adolescence: well-child visits, acute illnesses, emergencies and pediatric hospitalization when needed.

process.title: Book your appointment
process.desc: Via WhatsApp, phone or our online form.

process.title: Consultation
process.desc: The pediatrician examines your child and explains the diagnosis and treatment.

process.title: Follow-up
process.desc: We schedule the follow-up visits your child needs.

faq.q: Up to what age does the pediatrician see patients?
faq.a: Generally from birth to age 17.

faq.q: What if my child has an emergency at night?
faq.a: Come to the emergency room: we're open 24 hours a day, every day.

cirugia-general.name: General Surgery
cirugia-general.desc: Scheduled and emergency surgery with recovery in the same hospital.
cirugia-general.full: Surgeons who operate at Medipab perform scheduled and emergency procedures in the hospital's surgical area, supported by the laboratory, blood bank, inpatient care and intensive care when needed.

process.title: Assessment
process.desc: The surgeon evaluates your case and orders the necessary pre-operative tests.

process.title: Surgery
process.desc: Performed in the hospital's surgical area, with the laboratory and blood bank available.

process.title: Recovery
process.desc: Monitoring as an inpatient and a care plan to continue recovering at home.

faq.q: Can I have surgery with my own surgeon?
faq.a: If your surgeon operates at Medipab, yes. Ask us and we'll confirm.

faq.q: How long will I stay in the hospital?
faq.a: It depends on the procedure and how you recover. Your surgeon will tell you during the assessment.

ortopedia-traumatologia.name: Orthopedics and Trauma
ortopedia-traumatologia.desc: Fractures, sports injuries and bone and joint conditions.
ortopedia-traumatologia.full: We treat injuries and conditions of the bones, muscles and joints: from fractures and sprains that come through the emergency room to spine and joint problems that require consultation or surgery.

process.title: Assessment
process.desc: Physical exam and imaging to determine the type of injury.

process.title: Treatment
process.desc: Immobilization, medical treatment or surgery, depending on your case.

process.title: Follow-up
process.desc: Follow-up visits until you recover.

faq.q: If I break a bone, where should I go?
faq.a: Come directly to the emergency room: we're open 24 hours and have imaging in the hospital.

faq.q: Do I need an appointment for a non-urgent injury?
faq.a: Yes. Book your consultation via WhatsApp, phone or the online form.

consulta-externa.name: Specialty Outpatient Clinic
consulta-externa.desc: Over 50 medical specialists seeing patients at the hospital.
consulta-externa.full: Over 50 physicians from a range of specialties see patients at Medipab. Because you're seen inside the hospital, your specialist can order lab work and imaging, and schedule surgery or admission in the same place.
conditions: Referral to other specialties within the hospital

process.title: Tell us what you need
process.desc: We'll guide you to the right specialist for your case.

process.title: Scheduling
process.desc: We coordinate your appointment based on the doctor's availability.

process.title: Consultation
process.desc: Your specialist sees you and, if needed, orders tests right here.

faq.q: Which specialties do you have?
faq.a: In addition to those listed on this site, we have physicians from other specialties. Message us and we'll tell you whether we have the specialist you're looking for.

faq.q: How much does a consultation cost?
faq.a: The fee depends on each specialist; we'll let you know when you book.

laboratorio-clinico.name: Clinical Laboratory
laboratorio-clinico.desc: Lab testing inside the hospital for emergency, inpatient and outpatient patients.
laboratorio-clinico.full: Our laboratory processes tests for emergency, inpatient and outpatient patients, so your doctor has the results within the same hospital.
conditions: Complete blood count and blood chemistry

process.title: Order
process.desc: Your doctor orders the tests you need for your case.

process.title: Sample collection
process.desc: Trained staff collects the sample at the hospital.

process.title: Results
process.desc: Your doctor receives the results and reviews them with you.

faq.q: Do I need to fast?
faq.a: Some tests, such as glucose and cholesterol, require fasting. We'll tell you how to prepare when you book.

faq.q: Can I get tests without a doctor's order?
faq.a: Ask us which tests you can have done directly.

imagenologia.name: Medical Imaging
imagenologia.desc: Diagnostic imaging within the same hospital.
imagenologia.full: The imaging department performs studies that support diagnosis in the emergency room, inpatient care and outpatient clinic, without you having to go anywhere else. Ask us about available studies.

process.title: Doctor's order
process.desc: Your doctor orders the imaging study you need.

process.title: The study
process.desc: We perform the study at the hospital.

process.title: Report
process.desc: Your doctor receives the result to continue your diagnosis.

faq.q: Which studies do you perform?
faq.a: Message or call us and we'll confirm whether we perform the study your doctor ordered.

faq.q: Do I need any preparation?
faq.a: Some studies require fasting or other preparation; we'll tell you when you book.

banco-de-sangre.name: Blood Bank
banco-de-sangre.desc: Blood products available for surgery, emergencies and intensive care.
banco-de-sangre.full: Having a blood bank inside the hospital lets us respond quickly when a patient needs a transfusion during surgery, an emergency or a stay in intensive care.

faq.q: Can I donate blood at Medipab?
faq.a: Contact us to learn about blood donation and its requirements.

farmacia.name: Pharmacy
farmacia.desc: A pharmacy open to the public inside the hospital.
farmacia.full: Besides supplying inpatients, our pharmacy serves the general public, so you can fill your prescription after a consultation or an emergency visit without looking for another pharmacy.
conditions: Prescriptions from consultations and the emergency room

faq.q: Can I buy there even if I'm not a hospital patient?
faq.a: Yes, the pharmacy is open to the general public.

ambulancia.name: Ambulance Service
ambulancia.full: We have an ambulance service to transport patients when their condition requires it. Call us to request it.

faq.q: What should I do in a serious emergency?
faq.a: Call 911. You can also call us to request our ambulance.

faq.q: Is there a charge for transport?
faq.a: Yes. The cost depends on the transfer; we'll let you know when you request it.

cat1Items.q: Do I need an appointment to be seen?
cat1Items.a: To see a specialist, yes — we recommend booking. For emergencies you don't need an appointment: we're open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

cat1Items.q: How can I book an appointment?
cat1Items.a: Via WhatsApp, by phone or with the form on our Appointments page. We'll confirm the specialist's availability.

cat1Items.q: I don't know which specialist I need. Can you help?
cat1Items.a: Yes. Tell us your symptoms or the reason for your visit and we'll suggest the right specialist.

cat1Items.q: Do the doctors work at the hospital?
cat1Items.a: Medipab works with over 50 medical specialists who see and treat their patients at the hospital, backed by the emergency room, inpatient care, laboratory and imaging.

cat2Items.a: The emergency room and inpatient care operate 24 hours a day, every day. The outpatient clinic is by appointment, according to each specialist's schedule.
Yes. Every inpatient has their own room.
Yes, inside the hospital and open to the general public.
In Pabellón de Arteaga, Aguascalientes. See our exact location and directions on the Contact page.

cat3Items.a: 24-hour emergency room, inpatient care, adult intensive care, NICU, obstetrics and gynecology, pediatrics, general surgery, orthopedics and trauma, specialty outpatient clinic, clinical laboratory, medical imaging, blood bank, pharmacy and ambulance.
Yes. We have adult intensive care and a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU).

cat3Items.q: Do you handle vaginal deliveries and C-sections?
cat3Items.a: Yes, with obstetrics, pediatrics and a NICU in the same hospital.

cat3Items.q: Do you have an ambulance service?
cat3Items.a: Yes. Call us to request it. In a serious emergency you can also call 911.

cat4Items.a: We see self-pay patients and patients from insurers we have agreements with. Contact us to confirm whether your insurer has a current agreement with Medipab.

cat4Items.q: What payment methods do you accept?
cat4Items.a: We'll let you know the costs and payment methods when you book or at admissions.
Yes, we issue Mexican electronic invoices (CFDI). Request one at the cashier with your tax information.
